sources.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory
sources.locator: Complete §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 100–110, including surrounding definitions, posterior-risk calculation, minimax definition, and the randomization-removal discussion.

contents.name: §5.1: action spaces, nonnegative loss, decision rules, and expected-loss risk
§5.1 Definition 5.1: randomized decisions and integration of loss against the action law
contents.reason: The local definition states the two-stage kernel integral and cites the batch-2 action-law proof for measurability and extended nonnegative values.

contents.name: §5.1 Example 5.1: zero-one loss for binary testing
contents.reason: The binary loss is used in an explicit finite model; all risks are calculated locally.

contents.name: §5.1 Example 5.2: squared-error and absolute-error point-estimation losses
contents.reason: The squared-error loss is used in an explicit finite Bernoulli example; its risk is calculated locally. Absolute-error loss is not needed in this assigned inventory.

contents.name: §5.2 Definition 5.2: pointwise risk domination and admissibility
§5.2 Theorem 5.1: Rao–Blackwell conditional-risk reduction
contents.reason: Rao–Blackwellization is outside the MSF-03 inventory and is not used as a supplier.

contents.name: §5.2 Theorem 5.2: randomization removal for convex loss
contents.reason: The printed statement omits conditions needed for its action expectation. The controlling design supplies the closed convex finite-dimensional action, finite first moment, and barycenter-in-action hypotheses; the local proof uses an explicit integral-Jensen lemma and does not rely on Martin’s proof as printed.

contents.name: §5.3.1: prior-integrated risk and posterior-risk minimization
contents.reason: The local theorem supplies a measurable posterior minimizer, standard-Borel disintegration, nonnegative Tonelli argument, and comparison against every randomized rule.

contents.name: §5.3.2 Definition 5.5: maximum risk and minimax rules

sources.title: Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems
sources.locator: Complete 13-page note; inspected §§4.1–4.3 and §5, PDF pp. 7–13, including the decision-problem setup, expected-loss risk, examples, and global risk comparisons.

contents.name: §§4.1–4.2: decision space, loss, nonrandomized rule, and risk as expected loss
§4.3 Theorem 1: preference representation by expected loss
contents.reason: The printed display has the same P2 expectation on both sides, so it cannot express the claimed comparison. It is not used.

contents.name: §5: global comparisons by admissibility, Bayes risk, and minimax risk
§5, PDF p. 11: constant estimator with zero risk at one mean and poor risk away from it
contents.reason: That source example is not a domination claim. The planned dominated-constant example is instead verified in a two-point Bernoulli model where a data rule has risk zero at both parameters.

contents.name: §§4.1 and 5: binary testing, squared-error estimation, and global risk tradeoffs
contents.reason: These examples motivate the finite zero-one and squared-error cases; all probability masses and risk comparisons are checked locally.
